subject.title: fix: bound Codex cost scans on giant session corpora

question: Should local token-cost history eventually include every completed Codex rollout by using resumable bounded parsing, or is permanent omission of rollouts above 256 MiB an acceptable default behavior?
rationale: The implementation makes a deliberate user-visible accuracy tradeoff rather than a purely mechanical bug fix. Repository evidence proves the availability benefit, but cannot determine whether incomplete cost history is acceptable for existing users after upgrade.

options.title: Require eventual accounting
options.body: Replace the permanent oversized-file skip with resumable or chunked bounded parsing so each refresh remains safe while completed rollout costs eventually enter history.

options.title: Accept incomplete history explicitly
options.body: Keep the hard skip, but add a visible incomplete-history state and a supported recovery/configuration path so users are not silently shown partial totals.

options.title: Pause for product design
options.body: Defer the PR until the intended accuracy and availability contract for very large local rollout files is confirmed.

recommendation.title: Require eventual accounting
recommendation.body: Replace the permanent oversized-file skip with resumable or chunked bounded parsing so each refresh remains safe while completed rollout costs eventually enter history.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product-contract decision about the menu-bar cost-history feature rather than a narrow implementation detail.
